values.eyebrow: Strength and conditioning in Kelham Island
values.title: Get strong in a room that knows your name
values.text: Anvil Yard is an independent gym in an old Sheffield file works. Eight racks, six platforms, 46 coached classes a week and a coach on the floor from open to close.
values.note: First week free. No joining fee, no contract.

image.alt: A coach watching a member set up for a deadlift in the main hall

values.title: What members lift when they start, and four months later
values.intro: Median numbers from the 138 members who finished Barbell Basics in 2025 and kept training three times a week.

values.title: Three ways to train under one roof
values.intro: Come to class, lift on your own or follow a programme written for you. Most members mix all three, and every membership includes a coach you can ask.

items.title: Coached classes
items.text: Forty-six classes a week, from Barbell Basics to Heavy Day, each capped at 12 lifters so the coach sees every rep.

items.title: Open gym
items.text: Eight racks, six platforms, sleds and a 20 metre track, open from 5:30 am on weekdays with a coach always on the floor.

items.title: Your own programme
items.text: Coached members get a 12 week plan built around their goal and a sit-down review with their coach every month.

values.title: One Saturday morning, frame by frame
values.intro: Member and photographer Jo Castell shot a roll of film during Kettlebell Flow and the open gym hour that followed.

image.alt: The roller door of the old file works going up at first light
Chalk bowls and kettlebells lined up along the brick wall
Twelve members swinging kettlebells in two rows
A member locking out a deadlift while a coach watches the bar path
Members drinking tea on the benches by the front desk

values.quote: I walked in unable to lift the empty bar off the floor properly. Ellie taught me in Barbell Basics, Tom wrote my programme, and in May I pulled 110 kg in front of a room that was shouting my name.
values.name: Hannah Brooks

values.title: Your first seven days are on us
values.text: Come to any class, use the open gym and sit down with a coach for half an hour. If it is not for you, you owe us nothing.
values.note: Bring trainers and a water bottle. We lend you everything else.

values.title: Lift heavy.
values.text: Six kinds of class, every day of the week, each one run by a coach who knows what you lifted last time. Pick a slot, turn up, and we handle the plan.

values.title: A week of classes, already on the calendar
values.intro: These seven run every week of the year. Barbell Basics, Engine and Lunch Lift also repeat on other days, so there is always a slot that fits a shift pattern.

days.title: Barbell Basics
days.text: Squat, press and deadlift taught from the empty bar. The place to start.

days.title: Engine
days.text: Rower, sled and carries in intervals. Done before most people are at work.

days.title: Heavy Day
days.text: Work up to one heavy set of three, with a coach on every platform.

days.title: Lunch Lift
days.text: Forty-five minutes, two lifts, back at your desk by half past one.

days.title: Engine
days.text: Friday is partner day. Bring a friend for free and share the sled.

days.title: Kettlebell Flow
days.text: Swings, get-ups and carries strung into long, steady sets.

days.title: Mobility Reset
days.text: Slow hips, shoulders and ankles work to undo the week. Open to non-members.

values.note: Every class is 60 minutes and capped at 12 lifters. Lunch Lift runs 45 minutes.

values.title: Each class has one job
values.intro: You do not need to pick a favourite. Most members do two strength classes and one conditioning class a week.

image.alt: Coach Ellie Marsh showing a beginner where to place the bar for a squat

items.label: Mon and Thu · 18:00
items.title: Barbell Basics
items.text: An eight week course that repeats all year. You learn the squat, press, bench and deadlift, add a little weight every session and leave with a logbook that proves it.

image.alt: Four members pushing sleds down the indoor track

items.label: Tue and Fri · 6:30
items.title: Engine
items.text: Conditioning without the burpees. Intervals on the rower, ski machine and sled, scaled so the new member and the county rower finish at the same time.

image.alt: A lifter standing up with a heavy squat while two spotters watch

items.label: Wed · 18:30
items.title: Heavy Day
items.text: For members with six months under the bar. One main lift, worked up to a heavy triple, then accessory work chosen by your coach.

image.alt: A row of members holding kettlebells overhead

items.label: Sat · 9:00
items.title: Kettlebell Flow
items.text: Priya strings six movements into unbroken ten minute sets. Lighter on the joints than it sounds and harder on the lungs than it looks.

values.intro: Answers from 212 members who joined between September 2025 and February 2026.

items.label: Feel stronger in everyday life
items.note: Stairs, shopping bags and picking up children came up most.

items.label: Hit a personal best in the first 12 weeks
items.note: Half of them in the deadlift.

items.label: Now train three times a week or more
items.note: Up from 34% on the day they joined.

values.title: Before your first class
values.intro: The six things people ask at the front desk.

items.question: Can I come if I have never lifted?
items.detail: Start with Barbell Basics. Everyone there is new too.

items.question: Do I need to book?
items.detail: Classes cap at 12, so book in the app up to 7 days ahead.

items.question: Do I need my own kit?
items.detail: Flat shoes and water. Belts, chalk and straps are on the wall.

items.question: Is there a late cancel fee?
items.detail: Cancel up to an hour before so someone on the waitlist gets in.

items.question: Are there showers?
items.detail: Four showers, lockers and fresh towels at the desk.

items.question: Classes for under 16s?
items.detail: Youth Barbell starts on Saturday 9 January 2027.

values.title: Book a free taster class
values.text: Pick any class this week and come as our guest. A coach meets you ten minutes early, shows you round and keeps an eye on you all session.

values.title: Train with people who lift what they teach
values.text: Every Anvil Yard coach holds a British Weightlifting or UKSCA qualification, competes or has competed, and still writes their own training in a paper logbook.
values.name: Maya Okafor

values.title: The six people who will know your numbers
values.intro: There is always at least one of them in the building. Their badges say what to ask them about.

values.title: “Nobody is too weak to start. That is the whole point.”
values.intro: Ellie Marsh joined as a member in 2019 and now runs Barbell Basics. She asked Maya why the gym still teaches every new member itself.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: You opened in 2017 with two racks and a kettle. Why a strength gym, in Sheffield, in a building with no heating?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Because every gym I had worked in sold access and hoped you would not turn up. I wanted the opposite: a place that notices when you miss a week.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People tell me they need to get fit before they join. What do you say to that?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Nobody is too weak to start. That is the whole point of a barbell: it goes down to 5 kg and up in half kilo steps.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: We cap classes at 12. We could fit 20 in the hall.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: At 12 I can watch every working set. At 20 I am a timekeeper. The cap costs us money and it is the best decision we ever made.

values.title: What it is like to be coached here
values.intro: Four members, four coaches, one thing in common: somebody was paying attention.

items.quote: Tom rewrote my programme around night shifts without me asking.
items.name: Callum Reid

items.quote: Ellie remembered my bad shoulder in week one and still asks about it.
items.name: Farah Aziz

items.quote: Priya makes a 6:30 Engine class feel like the best part of Tuesday.
items.name: Greg Lawton

items.quote: Dan got me squatting again eight months after knee surgery.
items.name: Ruth Adeyemi

values.title: Book time with a coach
values.intro: Any member or guest can book a coach by the session. Coached members get one technique session a month included.
values.note: Prices include VAT. Sessions run at 22 Mowbray Street and can be moved free of charge with 24 hours notice.

For rotating shifts: use them whenever the rota allows.

values.before: I paid for a chain gym for three years and went eleven times. Here I have
values.highlight: missed four sessions in two years
values.after: because somebody texts me when I do.
values.name: Callum Reid

values.title: The question everyone asks at the desk
values.featuredQuestion: What happens if I sign up and stop coming?
values.featuredAnswer:
We notice. If you miss ten days your coach sends a message, and if life has got in the way we freeze your membership for free rather than keep taking your money.

About one member in five uses a freeze each year. Almost all of them come back.

items.question: Is there a contract?
items.answer: No. Every membership is month to month and you can cancel with 14 days notice by email.

items.question: Do you offer discounts?
items.answer: Students, NHS staff and over 60s pay £10 less a month on any membership. Two people at one address save £15 between them.

items.question: Can I change membership later?
items.answer: Yes, at the start of any month. Most Coached members began on Classes.

items.question: Can I pay for a year?
items.answer: Yes. Twelve months paid up front costs the same as ten.

values.title: Train for a month. If you are not stronger, it is free.
values.text: Come three times a week for your first paid month and follow the plan. If your logbook does not show more weight on the bar at the end, we refund the month.

points.text: Full refund of your first paid month
Your logbook is the only proof we need

values.note: In nine years we have refunded three people, and two of them rejoined.
